method: Author tree from git archive@4ec961e (aisef2 aisef tests validation docs pyproject.toml) + the one closure-evidence file the kill file reads, added read-only with `git show 4ec961e:closure-evidence/v2/release/LEDGERLOCK-PROJECT.json > ...`. Each mutant built from the pristine module via validation.v2.mutation.mutants(src,'_declared',_enum_members(src,tree))[INDEX]; desc asserted == this batch entry; written over aisef2/app/bundle_cli.py, the ONE registered kill file run, restored after. Env: env with PATH=/usr/bin:/bin (opencode lives only at ~/.opencode/bin, unreachable; git at /usr/bin/git), HOME/TMPDIR/XDG_* under the tree, LANG/LC_ALL=C, PYTHONPATH=tree; nice -n 19 /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 -P -B -m unittest tests.v2.test_v21_migrate_semantics -q. Baseline unmutated: 51 tests OK.
measurement_result: All 8 mutants: 51 tests OK (kill file PASS) == SURVIVED by measurement, matching the campaign. No REFUTED-by-measurement. The kill file's _declared-form test (test_a_record_the_reader_cannot_take_is_none_and_never_nothing_changed, L217-251) pins the descriptive strings `when` (non-text) and `ref` (empty / non-text) as rejected-to-None, and every real probe (only file_artifact declares changes, at capability 3) declares `affects`/`classes`/`subject_absence` as TUPLES — so no case exercises an empty/non-text `before`/`after` and no case exercises a list-typed `affects`/`classes`; every mutant survives.

entries.group: well_formed early-return sentinel (False -> None); only consumer is all()
entries.grounds: Line 210 is the first guard of the nested `well_formed(sel)` (structure: sel not a Mapping, or missing one of {when,before,after}, or an extra key) returning False; mutated to return None. `well_formed` is a local function (def at bundle_cli.py:207) whose return value is read in EXACTLY one place, bundle_cli.py:216 `return rec if all(well_formed(sel) for sel in rec['affects']) else None`. `all()` coerces each element to bool: both False and None are falsy, and the only truthy return (True, line 214) is untouched. So for every input `all(...)` yields the identical bool, hence `_declared` returns the identical value (rec or None). The `-> bool` annotation is not enforced at runtime and no consumer inspects it. No observable difference anywhere. Kill-file run: 51 OK (SURVIVED).
consumers_checked: the only reader of well_formed's return: bundle_cli.py:216 `all(well_formed(sel) for sel in rec['affects'])` — None and False are both falsy under all(), so _declared's return is byte-identical
sole caller of _declared: _assess bundle_cli.py:249 reads only `rec is None` vs the mapping (L250/L255), never the inner sentinel
grep aisef2/ validation/ tests/ docs/ for other references to well_formed — none (nested local)
exceptions_checked: no exception: the value never escapes `all(...)`, which cannot tell None from False; EQUIVALENT is proven from the code, not merely unobserved

entries.group: tuple|list leniency narrowed to tuple-only (fail-closed; no declaration in-tree uses a list)
entries.grounds: Top-level guard, bundle_cli.py:202-203: `not isinstance(rec['affects'], (tuple, list))`. The mutant drops `list`, leaving `(tuple,)` — a record whose `affects` is a LIST is now rejected (return None, L204) where the original accepted it. Observable (verified: original accepts affects=[sel] -> rec; mutant returns None), so NOT equivalent. Direction is fail-closed: `_declared`->None makes _assess (bundle_cli.py:250-253) raise the `every`-catch-all for every contract of the probe (approval withheld), the safe side of the migrate rule (docstring L225-227, kill-file docstring L11). But nothing in-tree depends on a list `affects` being accepted: the only probe with declared changes is file_artifact, whose CAPABILITY_CHANGES[2]/[3] `affects` are TUPLES (file_artifact.py:227,232,247); no test builds a list `affects` (the kill file's `good` uses a tuple, L219; the 'a list' case at L249 is `capability_changes` itself being a list, a different check); the docstring 'affects lists selectors' (file_artifact.py:214) is English, not a type requirement. Kill-file run: 51 OK (SURVIVED) — test_every_probe... (L181-194) and test_the_six_come_out... (L613-625, via _exposure on the real LedgerLock record) both pass because the real record is a tuple. before/after string validation is untouched (verified: all still rejected).

entries.group: a descriptive string dropped from the non-empty-str check (before/after unpinned; sibling when/ref pinned)
entries.grounds: Second guard, bundle_cli.py:211: `all(isinstance(sel[k], str) and sel[k] for k in ('when','before','after','ref') if k in sel)`. The mutant drops element 1, `'before'`, from the iterated tuple -> `('when','after','ref')`, so a selector's `before` is no longer required to be a non-empty string. `before` is a REQUIRED key (first guard, L208 `{'when','before','after'} <= set(sel)`), so it is always present but now unvalidated; line 213 only checks the collection keys {classes,subject_absence}, never `before`. Verified: with the mutant a record whose selector has before='' or before=3 (a non-str) is ACCEPTED (returns rec) where the original returns None. This flips _declared from fail-closed to fail-open on a malformed record: _assess then takes the selective branch (bundle_cli.py:255-259) instead of the every-contract catch-all (L250-253), so fewer approvals are withheld, and it reads the bad `before` into the operator-facing change hit (L257 `'before': sel['before']`). The kill file deliberately pins the SIBLING descriptive strings — `when` ('a when that is not text', L239) and `ref` ('a ref that is empty' L240, 'a ref that is not text' L241) — as rejected-to-None, but has NO case for an empty/non-text `before` (or `after`), a symmetric coverage gap. Kill-file run: 51 OK (SURVIVED) — nothing exercises a malformed `before`. A reader (the migrate/seal approval carry-over via _exposure, and the operator who reads the change's `before` in the report) depends on this validation; a test is owed.

the fail-closed invariant: `a malformed record ... withholds` (kill-file docstring L11; _assess docstring L225-227) — accepting before='' violates it
